title: How many of each shape does a base five sum have?
description: Two numerals made of base five shapes are added by counting each kind of shape. The board looks for any shape that reaches five, and the sum is checked by value.
teaching_notes: One idea: count each kind of shape and swap only when a count reaches the base, which is five. Watch for students who swap when a count is below five.

source: Figure it Out (adding with landmarks, question 2)
video_script.why: The child uses the count-and-swap method of the Egyptian addition in the base five system, where five of a shape make one of the next.
video_script.substitution: The base is five, so a swap is made when a count reaches five, not ten.
video_script.anchor: the book's two numerals made of base five shapes, one on each side of a plus sign
video_script.payoff_line: The sum is four circles, three hexagons, three squares and four triangles.

final_answer.value: 4 circles, 3 hexagons, 3 squares and 4 triangles, which is 594
final_answer.spoken: four circles, three hexagons, three squares and four triangles, which is five hundred ninety four

hold_back: 4 circles, 3 hexagons, 3 squares and 4 triangles, which is 594
maths_rules: triangle 1, square 5, hexagon 25, circle 125; five of one make one of the next
first numeral: 1 circle, 2 hexagons, 1 square, 2 triangles = 125 + 50 + 5 + 2 = 182
second numeral: 3 circles, 1 hexagon, 2 squares, 2 triangles = 375 + 25 + 10 + 2 = 412
circles 1 + 3 = 4; hexagons 2 + 1 = 3; squares 1 + 2 = 3; triangles 2 + 2 = 4; none reaches 5, so no swap
video_script.design: One idea: swap only when a count reaches five. The two numerals stay on the board while the counts appear below them.

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book about adding in the base five system.
<bookmark mark='sym'/>A triangle is one, and a square is five. <bookmark mark='sym2'/>A hexagon is twenty five, and a circle is one hundred twenty five.

<bookmark mark='ask'/>We must add one circle, two hexagons, one square and two triangles. <bookmark mark='ask2'/>To it we add three circles, one hexagon, two squares and two triangles. How many of each shape will the sum have?

beats.on_screen: the question stays on the board with the empty box

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

beats.on_screen: five triangles slide into one square; five squares into one hexagon; the plan count each kind, then swap every five

marks.gather: the same kinds of shape are gathered together
marks.five: five of a shape slide into one of the next shape

narration: <bookmark mark='gather'/>We add as we did with Egyptian numerals. We count each kind of shape together.
<bookmark mark='five'/>Here, five of a shape make one of the next shape. Five is the count to watch for.

beats.on_screen: Given: 1 circle, 2 hexagons, 1 square, 2 triangles; 3 circles, 1 hexagon, 2 squares, 2 triangles
narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, one circle, two hexagons, one square and two triangles.
<bookmark mark='given2'/>The second numeral is three circles, one hexagon, two squares and two triangles.

beats.on_screen: To find: the sum in base 5 shapes

marks.find: the words the sum in shapes are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find their sum, written in shapes.
<bookmark mark='circles'/>Step one, count the circles and the hexagons. Circles come to one plus three, which is four.
<bookmark mark='hex'/>Hexagons come to two plus one, which is three.
<bookmark mark='squares'/>Step two, count the squares and the triangles. Squares come to one plus two, which is three.
<bookmark mark='tri'/>Triangles come to two plus two, which is four.

beats.on_screen: counts 4, 3, 3, 4: all below 5, so no swap

marks.below: the four counts are each ticked as below five

narration: <bookmark mark='below'/>Step three, look for a shape that reached five. The counts are four, three, three and four, which are all below five, so nothing is swapped.
<bookmark mark='check'/>Step four, check by value. The numerals are worth one hundred eighty two and four hundred twelve. Together they add to five hundred ninety four.
<bookmark mark='check2'/>Our shapes are worth five hundred, seventy five, fifteen and four. Those also add to five hundred ninety four.

beats.on_screen: Answer: 4 circles, 3 hexagons, 3 squares and 4 triangles, which is 594
narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>The sum is four circles, three hexagons, three squares and four triangles. It is worth five hundred ninety four.
